about: Jobs the minimum wage does not reach, read by src/core2/wage-floor.ts. The Fair Labor Standards Act leaves an elected official and the people on their personal staff or in policymaking posts (a mayor's department heads, a legislator's aides) out of 'employee', so a wage floor raises none of their pay. A job at an employer outside the town's own law keeps that law.
citation: 29 U.S.C. 203(e)(2)(C): an individual elected to public office, chosen by an elected official to serve on their personal staff, appointed to a policymaking position, or serving as an immediate adviser, is not an employee for the Act's wage rules.
